quickStartLead: Start by creating a new site.
quickStartIntro: The generator gives you a complete structure and a working example in one go, so you can focus on content instead of scaffolding.
quickStartCreateDesc: The fastest way to start is with the built-in generator.
quickStartCreateNote: The CLI will ask for a name, path, and a few defaults, then scaffold the site for you.
quickStartLayoutDesc: A typical site looks like this. src/pages holds page templates and logic, src/sites defines site variants, and public/__ASSETS__ is the shared entry for static assets.
quickStartLayoutTree:
.
|- public/
|  |- __ASSETS__/       # static assets (images, favicon, etc.)
|- src/
|  |- i18n/             # locale JSON files
|  |- pages/            # page templates & logic
|  |- sites/            # site variant scripts
|- package.json         # site package info
|- site.config.ts       # site config
|- tsconfig.json
quickStartStep1Desc: Scaffold a full structure with pages, i18n, sites, and config.
quickStartStep2Desc: Use the Nx dev command with site filters and custom ports.
quickStartStep3Desc: Ship optimized bundles and validate routes locally.
quickStartCommandsLead: Day-to-day work centers around dev, build, and preview. They all run through Nx for consistent behavior across projects.
quickStartDevDesc: Start the dev server with HMR enabled. It prints a preview URL so you can iterate quickly.
quickStartBuildDesc: Use build when you want a deployable output. Artifacts land in dist/ with minification and versioning applied based on your configuration.
quickStartPreviewDesc: Preview serves the built output from dist/ to simulate production locally. It is especially useful for validating routes, asset paths, and redirects.
quickStartOptionsNote: See CLI / Nx Reference for full option details.
quickStartModelLead: Think in three layers: pages become routes, i18n clones pages, and sites diversify outputs.
quickStartModelCard1Desc: Folders under src/pages map to routes; index.html + main.* define each page. Missing main.* falls back to src/pages/main.*.
quickStartModelCard2Desc: JSON packs in src/i18n generate per-language pages; use *.default.json to pick the default locale.
quickStartModelCard3Desc: Scripts in src/sites create independent site outputs and add site prefixes in dev.
quickStartModelCard4Desc: Use data-to in templates; for code, use virtual:route-manifest + manifestResolver with getPageContext.
quickStartPipelineLead: Build and dev follow a predictable pipeline so URLs stay correct across modes.
quickStartPipelineStep2: Clone pages for each locale from src/i18n.
quickStartPipelineStep3: Clone pages for each site script in src/sites.
quickStartPipelineStep4: Generate a route manifest and rewrite data-to links based on route.mode.
quickStartPipelineStep5: Inject controllers and emit bundled assets to dist/.

quickStartConfigItem1: route: mode, resolution, orientation, and useSiteAsPath.
quickStartConfigItem3: redirect & sitemap: language redirects and sitemap.xml.

conceptsTitle: Core concepts that shape every site
conceptsLead: From routing to page context, the SDK keeps structure predictable and extensible.
conceptRouteDesc: Choose tree for directory URLs or flat for single-level outputs.
conceptRouteWhat: Route mode defines how a folder path becomes an output URL. The SDK translates every page path using a single rule so links and assets stay coherent.
conceptRouteWhy: Different hosts prefer different shapes: tree mode aligns with folder-based URLs, while flat mode supports hosts that dislike nested paths.
conceptRouteReferenceNote: The route value is a reference derived from src/pages. Final URLs are shaped by route.mode, i18n, and site variants, so avoid hardcoding filenames in templates.
conceptRouteUse: match hosting constraints without rewriting templates
control language prefixes and file naming strategy
keep internal links consistent across dev and build
conceptRouteExampleTitle: How routes map in each mode
conceptRouteExampleMap:
src/pages/about/me/index.html -> /about/me/index.html (tree)
src/pages/about/me/index.html -> about_me.html (flat)
With i18n (en): /en/about/me/index.html (tree) or about_me_en.html (flat)
conceptPagesDesc: Pages live in src/pages with index.html + main.ts, or a shared entry.
conceptPagesWhat: A page is a folder with index.html (or index.ejs) and an optional main entry. The SDK turns this into a route and bundles page logic for you.
conceptPagesWhy: The convention reduces routing config and keeps structure predictable, so teams can scan the tree and understand URLs instantly.
conceptPagesPairNote: Each directory treats index.{html,ejs} as the route-defining template and main.{js,ts,jsx,tsx} as the entry script for that page. Think of them as a pair: index.* decides the route, main.* powers the page.
conceptPagesUse: share a single main entry across multiple pages
create route-based pages without extra router setup
conceptPagesExampleTree:
src/pages/
|- index.html
|- main.ts
|- about/
|  |- index.html
|  |- main.ts
|  |- me/
|     |- index.html
|     |- main.ts
conceptPagesHoistDesc: If a page folder does not include main.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}, the SDK falls back to src/pages/main.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}.
conceptPagesHoistTree:
src/pages/
|- main.ts            # shared entry (hoisted)
|- index.html         # page template for /
|- about/
|  |- index.html      # page template for /about
conceptPagesHoistNote: In this structure, both / and /about will use the shared src/pages/main.ts entry.
conceptI18nDesc: Drop JSON packs in src/i18n to auto-generate localized routes.
conceptI18nWhat: Every JSON pack becomes a locale build. The SDK clones pages per language and injects i18n, lang, and defaultLang into templates.
conceptI18nWhy: You avoid duplicate templates and still ship per-locale URLs, which is essential for SEO and localized campaigns.
conceptI18nUse: switch languages via data-locale without custom routing
share templates while varying content by locale
conceptI18nDefaultNote: To set the default language, name one file with the *.default.json suffix (only one default file is allowed).
conceptSitesDesc: Add scripts in src/sites to generate dedicated site versions.
conceptSitesWhat: A site script defines a variant build. The SDK duplicates pages per site and injects the site context, producing independent outputs.
conceptSitesWhy: Campaigns often need parallel variants (brand, region, A/B). Site scripts let you ship each variant without forking templates.
conceptSitesDevNote: In dev mode, the site name appears as a URL prefix so you can switch variants quickly. In build output, each site is emitted into its own directory so variants can be deployed independently.
conceptSitesUse: develop multiple variants in one codebase
ship separate builds per site script
scope controllers and content by site
conceptContextDesc: Read lang, site, and route with getPageContext in JS or templates.
conceptContextWhat: Page context is a runtime snapshot of the current route, locale, and site. It lets templates and scripts adapt based on where the page is rendered.
conceptContextWhy: A single code path can branch by route or locale without duplicating files or wiring state across pages.
conceptContextUse: render sections conditionally by locale or site
build programmatic navigation with the route manifest
attach behavior only on specific routes
conceptFlowLead: Each layer builds on the previous one to produce consistent URLs and predictable builds.
conceptFlowSteps: Pages define a base route map from src/pages.
i18n duplicates pages per locale and injects language context.
Sites duplicate pages per variant and attach site context.
The route manifest is generated from the expanded pages.
data-to links are rewritten using route.mode and the manifest.
Controllers are injected and assets are emitted to dist/.
conceptProgressLead: Build the structure step by step and watch how URLs evolve.
conceptProgressStep1Desc: Start with src/pages only. Each folder becomes a route in tree mode.
conceptProgressStep2Desc: Each locale duplicates pages. Default locale has no prefix; others do.
conceptProgressStep3Desc: Each site script duplicates the whole site. URLs gain a site prefix in dev.
conceptProgressSiteNote: Sites are independent outputs. They can be deployed separately, and hidden routes or controllers can target a single site without affecting others.
conceptExampleLinkNote: In templates, use data-to like /about/team; the SDK rewrites links based on route.mode, locale, and site.
conceptsNextDesc: Learn how to compose pages with EJS and reusable components.

templatingLead: All .html and .ejs files are treated as EJS templates.
templatingIntro: You can embed data and logic directly in markup without switching formats.
templatingVarsList: `$cmp`: helper to resolve EJS component paths.
`_data`: reference to the root data object (pass to components).
templatingVarsWhat: All HTML/EJS files are rendered as templates. The SDK injects route, locale, site, and env data into each render.
templatingVarsWhy: This keeps templates mode-aware without manual wiring, so a single template works across locales and variants.
templatingVarsUse: branch by route or site without extra state
access env values in both EJS and JS
templatingComponentsDesc: Create reusable fragments such as header.ejs or footer.ejs, then include them through $cmp so paths resolve consistently.
templatingComponentsLocal: For local components, use a path without @ and it resolves to src/components/.
templatingComponentsCross: For cross-project usage, prefix the path with @ to resolve through the monorepo.
templatingDataDesc: When including components, pass _data to preserve the full root context.
templatingDataWhy: It avoids variable shadowing. _data always points at the root template data, so even if a component defines lang, you can still access _data.lang reliably.
templatingGeneratorDesc: Use the component generator to scaffold component templates. Output varies by framework, but the generator keeps the structure consistent across sites.
templatingGeneratorOptions: `name` (required): component name. Must start with a letter, and can include letters, numbers, and `-`.
`framework`: `none` (default), `vue`, or `react` to pick the component template set.
`useTs`: when false, generated files are converted to JS/JSX.
`project`: target Nx project (must be an application). When set, the generator resolves the component folder from the project's site.config sourcePath.components.
`path`: explicit output path. Overrides the project path if provided.
templatingGeneratorOutputDesc: For framework: none, you get index.ejs with index.ts (or index.js when useTs is false). For framework: vue, you get a single-file *.vue. For framework: react, you get *.tsx (or *.jsx when useTs is false).
templatingGeneratorLocationDesc: If project is set, output goes to ${projectRoot}/${sourcePath.components}. If path is set, it uses that directly. Otherwise it falls back to the @landing-page-sdk/assets project's components folder.
templatingAssetsDesc: Place static assets under public/__ASSETS__ and reference them with the /__ASSETS__ prefix. The SDK rewrites paths at build time based on your route/output settings, so the same markup works across different modes.
templatingNextDesc: Learn how to keep URLs stable across tree/flat output modes.
routingLead: Route mode, resolution, and link helpers ensure URLs remain correct across deploy targets.
routingModesDesc: Tree mode mirrors folders; flat mode flattens output into single-level files.
routingModesWhat: Route mode defines how page paths map to output URLs, affecting folders, filenames, and locale prefixes.
routingModesWhy: Different hosts have different routing capabilities. A single switch keeps templates stable across deployments.
routingModesUse: control language prefix vs filename suffix
keep URLs consistent across dev and build
routingDataToDesc: Use data-to for internal links so the SDK can rewrite them per mode.
routingDataToWhat: data-to is a declarative internal link. The SDK rewrites it based on route.mode, locale, and site.
routingDataToWhy: It prevents broken links when switching tree/flat or changing locale rules.
routingDataToNote: Use route references like /about/me. Avoid concrete outputs such as /about/index.html, ../about, or ./about_en.html—the SDK resolves the final URL based on mode, locale, and site.
routingDataToUse: create links that survive route mode changes
routingManifestDesc: Resolve URLs at runtime using the route manifest and page context.
routingManifestWhat: The route manifest is an indexed map of all resolved URLs, generated during build/dev.
routingManifestWhy: When routing is dynamic, hardcoded URLs become fragile. The manifest guarantees correct output.
routingManifestUse: resolve URLs by route + locale + site
routingResolutionDesc: Switch between relative and absolute links with route.resolution.
routingResolutionWhat: Resolution controls whether generated links are relative (rel) or absolute (abs).
routingResolutionWhy: Relative links are portable; absolute links are explicit for canonical URL needs.
routingResolutionUse: ensure canonical URLs in multi-site setups
routingOrientationDesc: Tree mode supports dir or file orientation for link output.
routingOrientationWhat: Orientation decides whether tree mode uses /path/ or /path/index.html links.
routingOrientationWhy: Some hosts require explicit filenames; others prefer directory-style URLs.
routingOrientationNote: Only applies when route.mode is tree. Flat mode always outputs file-based links.
routingOrientationUse: satisfy hosts that don't support clean URLs
routingSitePathDesc: Use route.useSiteAsPath when hosting multiple sites under one domain.
routingSitePathWhat: useSiteAsPath prepends the site name to routes and assets when using absolute paths.
routingSitePathWhy: It keeps multiple variants isolated under the same domain without manual path management.
routingSitePathNote: This only affects absolute paths; relative links are already site-local.
routingSitePathUse: host multiple variants under one root
routingSitePathAssetNote: Assets also gain the site segment when using absolute paths:
routingHiddenDesc: Exclude specific routes by site or language from build output.
routingHiddenWhat: Hidden routes are filtered out of output, manifests, and sitemaps based on rules.
routingHiddenWhy: It lets you disable pages per site or locale without deleting source files.
routingHiddenUse: roll out pages gradually by locale
routingNextDesc: Attach scripts without manually editing every template.
controllerLead: Controller injection attaches scripts to pages without manual edits. The SDK resolves targets and injects controllers either into page entries (bundle mode) or directly into HTML (inline mode).
controllerTargetModelDesc: Controllers are matched per page using the page’s route reference, language, and site variant. A page only receives a controller when all target conditions match. Redirect pages are excluded from injection.
controllerTargetModelNote: Default behavior is conservative: if you omit targets, the default route is ['/'], so only the root page matches. To apply a controller to all routes, pass an empty list: routes: [].
controllerTargetConditionsDesc: Use a structured target to refine injection by route, language, and site variant. All conditions are ANDed.
controllerBundleDesc: Bundle mode injects controllers into the page entry. Placement controls whether the import appears before or after existing code.
controllerInlineDesc: Inline mode injects a script tag into HTML. Choose head or body, and place before or after existing content.
controllerInlineBundleDesc: Inline scripts are bundled by default. Set bundle: false to inject raw source, or override esbuild options to control minification and targets.
controllerNextDesc: Dive deeper into output settings, redirects, and sitemap options that pair with controller injection.
advancedLead: site.config.js exposes rich options to customize build behavior. The sections below focus on the configuration you’ll reach for most often.
advancedOutputDesc: Controls format, minification, and output location for build artifacts.
advancedOutputFields: `minify`: true (default), false, a single target, or a list of targets.
`versioning`: hard (default) for hashed filenames, soft for query hash.
`assetsResolution`: abs (default) or rel for HTML asset paths.
`threshold`: size warning threshold in bytes for media assets.
advancedOutputAssetsDesc: Place static assets under public/__ASSETS__/ and reference them as /__ASSETS__/foo.png. Plugins rewrite to absolute or relative paths according to assetsResolution and apply hard/soft versioning.
advancedRedirectDesc: Auto-detect browser language and redirect to the correct locale.
advancedRedirectFields: `enable` (default true): add a root redirect page for multi-lang sites.
`transform(page)`: hook to mutate redirect page DOM (JSDOM window).
advancedSitemapDesc: Generates sitemap.xml (and an index for multi-lang).
advancedMockDesc: Powered by vite-plugin-mock. By default it reads from @landing-page-sdk/assets/mock. Set mock: false to disable, or point to a custom directory such as mock: 'src/my-mocks'.
advancedMockNote: You can also point to a workspace path such as mock: '@sites/project-a/mocks'.
advancedEnvDesc: Values under env are injected into the client.
advancedEnvNote: Use it in JavaScript via import.meta.env.API_ENDPOINT and in EJS via <%= env.API_ENDPOINT %>.
advancedNextDesc: Review the map or jump to another chapter.

spaLead: The SDK is page-first: HTML templates define pages and output routes, and your JavaScript enhances those pages. When you bring in a SPA framework, you are mounting an app inside a page—not replacing the routing model.
spaMountTitle: Mount point in the page template
spaMountDesc: Your template provides the HTML shell (title, meta, assets) and exposes a root element for the framework to mount into. This keeps routing predictable and output static-friendly.
spaBootstrapTitle: Bootstrap the framework in the page entry
spaBootstrapDesc: Each page can have a `main.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}` entry. The entry imports the framework app and mounts it to the template root. This keeps the SDK’s page structure intact while letting the framework own the interactive UI.
spaPluginsDesc: Framework support is provided through Vite plugins. Add the framework plugin(s) in `site.config` and keep the rest of the SDK structure unchanged.
spaRoutingDesc: The SDK already handles page routing and output, so a full SPA router is often unnecessary for landing pages. Use the route manifest to resolve internal links consistently across tree/flat, locales, and site variants.
spaI18nDesc: The SDK exposes language packs through `getPageContext`. Wrap it in a framework-friendly helper so your components can consume localized text without re-implementing the SDK’s i18n rules.
spaWhereDesc: See `examples/vue` for a full working reference. The key files are:
configRefLead: This is the complete reference for `site.config.{js,ts}`. Use it when you need exact types, defaults, or edge-case behavior.
configRefShapeDesc: The config is a plain object and can be validated with the `SiteConfig` type.
configRefRouteDesc: Controls how pages map to output paths and how internal links are rendered. You can set a simple mode or a full option object.
configRefRouteFields: `resolution` (default 'rel'): render internal links as relative or absolute.
`orientation` (default 'dir'): directory vs file links (tree mode only).
`useSiteAsPath` (default false): prefix site name into absolute paths.
configRefOutputDesc: Controls minification, versioning, asset paths, and output directory.
configRefOutputFields: `minify` (default true): controls which targets are minified.
`threshold`: size warning threshold (bytes) for media assets.
configRefOutputDefaults: Defaults: `minify: true`, `versioning: 'hard'`, `assetsResolution: 'abs'`, `dist: {workspaceRoot}/dist`. If you set a relative `dist` (for example, `./dist`), it resolves from the project root.
configRefRedirectDesc: Controls language redirect page generation. Set to `false` to disable redirect pages entirely.
configRefRedirectFields: `enable` (default true): generate a root redirect page for multi-lang sites.
`transform(page)`: hook to mutate the redirect page DOM.
configRefRedirectDefaults: Defaults: `enable: true`, `stub: false`. `transform` lets you adjust the redirect page DOM.
configRefPluginsDesc: Vite plugins for the site build. This is how SPA frameworks integrate with the SDK.
configRefEnvDesc: Arbitrary environment values injected into the client.
configRefEnvNote: Access in JavaScript via `import.meta.env.KEY`, and in EJS via `<%= env.KEY %>`.
configRefControllerDesc: Declare controller injections by route, language, and site.
configRefSitemapFields: `exclude`: route matchers to exclude from sitemap.
`useSiteAsPath` (default false): prefix site name into sitemap URLs.
configRefMockDefaults: Defaults to `@landing-page-sdk/assets/mock`. Set to `false` to disable, or provide a custom path.
configRefMockNote: The path can be a project-relative directory or a workspace alias.
cliLead: All SDK tasks are exposed as Nx targets. Always run them through `npx nx` so behavior stays consistent across projects.
cliTargetsDesc: Example projects expose three primary targets. Replace the project name with your own.
cliTargetsAlt: You can also use the explicit run form:
cliOptionsDesc: These targets map to the `@landing-page-sdk/core:vite` executor. Options are passed to the target:
cliOptionHost: host for the dev server. Accepts `true` or a host string.
cliOptionPort: port for the dev or preview server.
cliOptionVerbose: print verbose logs (executor, Vite plugins, mock middleware).
cliOptionsNote: Notes: `dev`, `build`, and `preview` are the same executor with different `mode` values. `--sites` applies to build and preview as well.
deployLead: The SDK outputs a static site, so deployment is mostly about choosing URL shape, asset paths, and language handling.
deployOutputDesc: Build artifacts are written to `{workspaceRoot}/dist` by default. You can override this with `output.dist`. If you set a relative path (for example, `./dist`), it resolves from the project root because the executor changes `cwd` before running Vite.
deployRouteDesc: Route shape affects emitted files and final URLs. Use `tree` for directory-style URLs and `flat` when your host prefers single-level files.
deploySubpathDesc: If your site lives under a subpath (for example, `https://example.com/landing/`), use relative assets and links so output works at any depth.
deployMultiSiteDesc: Site variants are independent outputs. In dev, a site prefix helps you switch and browse variants quickly. In build output, each site is emitted into its own directory (for example, `dist/site-a/**`), so each variant can be deployed separately.
deployMultiSiteNote: If you host multiple sites under a shared domain, enable `route.useSiteAsPath` so absolute links and assets include the site prefix.
deployI18nDesc: For multi-language sites, you can generate redirect pages that detect the browser language and forward to the correct locale.
deployI18nNote: `stub: true` also creates per-route stubs (for example, `/about/me` -> `/en/about/me`), which helps when the host can’t handle dynamic redirects.
deploySitemapDesc: Use the sitemap option to generate `sitemap.xml` during build. You can set a base URL directly:
